subject: OrbitHealth Invoice estimate & cost model (post-demo follow-up)
messages:
From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
To: Sara Liu <sara.liu@orbithealth.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>, Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Aug 2027 15:23:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo recap & next steps - token volumes / pricing

Hi Sara -

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from our side and a couple of asks so we can finalize an initial invoice estimate:

- Ask: please confirm the monthly active usage you expect for the clinical summarization flow (tokens measured after prompt prep): you mentioned ~150-250M tokens/mo as a steady-state range; is that accurate?
- Model: you preferred the redwood-turbo-3b-ops variant for latency; we modeled costs for that and a fallback gpt-3-ml-8k variant for peak capacity.
- Budget signal: you indicated an initial internal target around $150k- $220k/mo for inference; can you confirm whether this is a firm budget range or flexible depending on unit economics?

Next steps I propose:
1) You confirm a working token estimate (best guess for month 1 and steady-state).
2) I'll send a short invoice estimate + cost model showing unit economics (cost per 1M tokens), recommended discounts for committed volume, and an example monthly invoice.
3) If procurement wants a clean invoice PDF and a line-item cost spreadsheet, we'll attach that and include payment/PO terms.

I'm attaching a rough calculator and a one-page cost breakdown (work-in-progress) - will finalize after you confirm volumes.

Thanks -
Sean Gallagher
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
(sean.gallagher@redwood.com)

Attachments: OrbitHealth_pricing_calculator.csv, token_cost_breakdown.pdf

From: Sara Liu <sara.liu@orbithealth.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Garcia <t.garcia@orbithealth.com>, procurement@orbithealth.com
Date: Wed, 11 Aug 2027 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo recap & next steps - token volumes / pricing

Hey Sean -

Thanks for the summary. Confirming the usage assumptions:
- Month 1 (pilot): ~60M tokens (few hundred users, heavy sampling)
- Month 2-3 ramp: 120-160M tokens
- Steady-state (Q4 goal): 200M tokens/mo (this is the number leadership is targeting)

Budget: leadership gave a target ceiling of $220k/mo for inference as part of the Q4 forecast but they asked us to prioritize staying under ~$180k/mo if possible. So there is some flexibility but prefer a plan that lands at or below $180k with a path to $220k if we need capacity/throughput.

Procurement (cc) will want a line-item invoice and a breakdown of what's included (platform fees, per-token inference, storage of KV cache, support/SLAs). Tom - please loop in any specific PO/accounting info.

Sara
VP Product | OrbitHealth

From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
To: Sara Liu <sara.liu@orbithealth.com>, procurement@orbithealth.com
Cc: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>, Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 11 Aug 2027 11:02:00 -0700
Subject: OrbitHealth - Initial invoice estimate & unit economics (attached)

Hi Sara / Tom / procurement team -

Attached is the initial invoice estimate and cost model based on the volumes you confirmed. Highlights up front so it's easier to scan:

- Steady-state target: 200M tokens/mo
- Proposed list pricing (hosted / standard): $1,200 per 1M tokens (this is list before committed-volume discount)
- Example unit economics we modeled:
  * Platform & infra cost to Redwood (estimated): $500 per 1M tokens
  * Contribution margin (before discount): $700 per 1M tokens at list pricing
- Committed 12-month discount tiers (recommended):
  * 10-25% off list depending on committed volume and payment terms
  * Example: 15% discount => $1,020 per 1M tokens => $204k/mo at 200M tokens
  * Example: 20% discount + annual prepay => $960 per 1M => $192k/mo at 200M tokens
- Pilot pricing option (Month 1-3) we can offer: $900 per 1M tokens for up to 160M tokens during ramp to help meet the $180k/mo signal. That would put 200M tokens steady-state at $180k/mo if you convert 40M tokens to a different (metered) line - we can model split-line items in the invoice.

Attachments included: OrbitHealth_Invoice_Estimate_Q3_v2.xlsx (line-item invoice + monthly example), OrbitHealth_pricing_calculator.csv (CSV calculator you can edit), token_cost_breakdown.pdf (one-page unit economics). Link to editable drive folder: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1A2b3OrbitHealthPricing

Ask: can procurement confirm whether a PO will cover the first quarter and whether payment will be monthly net-30 or an annual prepay? That determines the discount we can lock in.

If useful, Dev (cc) is available tomorrow for a short call to review the cost model assumptions (kernel-level perf, tokenization overhead, KV cache size assumptions).

Best,
Sean Gallagher
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Attachments: OrbitHealth_Invoice_Estimate_Q3_v2.xlsx, OrbitHealth_pricing_calculator.csv, token_cost_breakdown.pdf

From: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
To: Sara Liu <sara.liu@orbithealth.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
Cc: Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 12 Aug 2027 08:34:00 -0700
Subject: Re: OrbitHealth - Initial invoice estimate & unit economics (attached)

Hi Sara -

Quick tech note to justify the assumptions in the cost model:
- Tokenization: we modeled an average of 2.8 tokens per word for the summarization prompts you showed; prompt + response avg = ~120 tokens per call.
- KV cache hit assumptions: we assumed a 22% effective hit rate across repeating user prompts which reduces total generated tokens by ~18% compared to raw requests.
- Model perf: redwood-turbo-3b-ops on A100/RTX-class infra delivers ~1,250 tokens/sec sustained with batching; we used that to model concurrency and latency SLO headroom.
- Storage + KV egress: small line item (~$0.02 per 1M tokens modeled) included in platform cost.

If you want a version where we swap in the gpt-3-ml-8k variant (better quality for long clinical context), the per-1M token cost increases by ~35% in our model - happy to produce that comparison in the spreadsheet.

-Dev
Principal Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
